text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1 alert for Equinox Corp (tenant: equinox-prod, dedicated-vpc). Symptoms: sustained packet loss and TCP retransmits from us-east-1 egress to customer DX. Pager to @Maya Chen @Ashish Patel. Channel created for coordination. thread_ts=2190012345
Maya Chen: I'm taking primary. Noted ~40% packet loss at the edge. Customer on dedicated warm capacity in eu-west standby. Equinox runs critical checkout path.
Ashish Patel: Joining. Can someone paste recent L7/L4 stats? Need to rule out app-level errors.
Eli Rocha: Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/eqnx/pool_us-east?from=-20m
Eli Rocha: L7 5xx not high on origin containers; rather we see heavy TCP retransmits and flow drops between gwy-us-east-2 and the customer's DirectConnect.
Frida Morales: Edge gateway logs show interface flapping (gwy-us-east-2b -> peer). BGP withdraw at 09:06 UTC and intermittent restores since.
Kenji Sato: Confirmed on router: physical interface with carrier had link flaps at 09:05. Opened ticket with carrier NOC (ref CN-8427). ETA unknown.
Maya Chen: Because Equinox is enterprise with SLA, propose immediate mitigation: route-control weighted shift to eu-west warm pool (no DNS flip yet) with sticky-session preservation. Also spin up extra warm replicas in eu-west to absorb increased load. Objections?
Ashish Patel: Agreed. Weighted shift avoids cache poisoning and minimizes session churn. We should keep old path for in-flight sessions until stable. TTL-based DNS change is risky given caches.
Eli Rocha: Route-control supports region weights and preserves X-RW-SESSION affinity for 24h. We'll do staged: 10% -> 40% -> 100% if metrics good.
Frida Morales: Kicking scale:
```
redwood cli pools scale --tenant equinox --region eu-west-1 --profile dedicated-warm --delta 10
```
Frida Morales: Launching 10 hot replicas (image v2026.02). Expected ready in ~4-6 minutes.
Kenji Sato: Need to add peering allowlist on eu-west edges for Equinox CIDRs. Applying: `infractl firewall add --region eu-west-1 --tenant equinox --cidr 10.92.0.0/16`
Kenji Sato: Firewall rule applied.
Ashish Patel: Applying route-control initial split (10% eu-west). API call: POST /rc/tenants/equinox/split {"weights":[{"region":"eu-west-1","weight":10},{"region":"us-east-1","weight":90}]}
incident-bot: route-control change recorded by deploy-bot: rc-change-219001-a1. Initiator: Ashish Patel. Audit: https://audit.redwood/rc/rc-change-219001-a1
Maya Chen: Canary active. Monitor 5xx, P50/P95 latency, and backend TCP retransmit rate. Post any anomalies here.
Eli Rocha: Canary looks healthy: eu-west traffic 200s, P95 +8ms. Retransmit rate for eu-west below 1%. Original us-east path still showing drops.
Frida Morales: Warm replicas booted: 10/10 ready. KV cache cold; expecting warm-up hit rate to ramp.
Kenji Sato: BGP issues still present toward DC provider. No ETA. We should prepare a DNS plan as fallback in case route-control fails.
Maya Chen: Agreed. We'll try to complete full shift via route-control first. If route-control is unable to reach 100% or carrier restores with instability, we'll coordinate emergency DNS flip with TTL 60. Customer must sign off.
Ashish Patel: Moving to 40% now (scheduled ramp).
incident-bot: route-control weights updated: eu-west:40% us-east:60% (rc-change-219001-a2)
Eli Rocha: After ramp: overall 5xx for the tenant dropped from ~35% -> 7%. Eu-west nodes handling requests fine. KV miss rate initially high but decaying (now ~30%).
Frida Morales: Observed an unrelated job: async backup writes failing against eu-west backup endpoint (502). Root cause: backup endpoint env var still pointing to us-east host. Applying hotfix to backup config.
Maya Chen: Hotfix deployed. Backup job retries succeeding. No data lost per preliminary checks.
Ashish Patel: Ready to push to 100% in 15 minutes provided metrics stable. Any blockers?
Kenji Sato: Double-check session affinity behavior for long-lived websockets. Route-control uses sticky token; should survive. I will validate websocket health-checks on eu-west.
Maya Chen: Notifying Equinox primary ops: "We are shifting traffic to eu-west warm pool using our routing layer to mitigate packet loss in us-east. We expect gradual routing over 30m. No DNS change unless necessary. Will update every 15m."
Equinox-Support: Acknowledged. Prefer to avoid changing DNS. Approved emergency DNS flip if it prevents revenue impact.
Ashish Patel: Proceeding 100% now.
incident-bot: route-control weights updated: eu-west:100% us-east:0% (rc-change-219001-a3).
Eli Rocha: Post-shift telemetry: tenant 5xx <1%, user latency stable. Edge load eu-west +15%. KV miss rate dropping.
Frida Morales: Running quick config audit to ensure no stale NATs or route leaks. Also checking for sticky session cookies preservation.
Kenji Sato: Audit complete: no stale NATs. Websocket connections properly proxied.
Maya Chen: Notifying Equinox: shift complete, monitoring. We'll keep both warm pools up for 4 hours and then reassess.
Ashish Patel: Creating incident ticket & postmortem stub. Owners: Maya Chen (incident lead), Kenji Sato (oncall followup). Action items:
- Carrier NOC follow-up and RCA for BGP flaps (CN-8427).
- Automate auto-fallback: if route-control cannot reach 100% in X minutes, optionally trigger DNS flip with TTL 60 and customer opt-in.
- Improve KV cache priming strategy for cross-region shifts.
Maya Chen: On-call handoff scheduled 10:30 UTC to Kenji Sato. I'll prepare handoff notes with links to dashboards, route-control changelist, and audit logs.
incident-bot: Reminder: oncall-handoff at 10:30 UTC. Handoff reference: https://incidents.redwood/2190012345/handoff
Kenji Sato: Taking handoff at 10:30. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: Great teamwork. Closing active pager. Keeping thread open for postmortem updates.
